hook_text: Six packets of biscuits at 250 grams each. Is that more or less than a kilogram? Do it in your head.
clip_script: Bakery at the Paarl market. Biscuits in 250 gram packets. 250 grams is a quarter of a kilogram, because 1 000 divided by 4 is 250. Four packets make 1 kilogram. Six packets? 6 times 250 is 1 500 grams: one and a half kilograms. More! Now the potatoes, 2 kilograms 500 grams, plus onions, 750 grams. Change to grams: 2 500 plus 750 is 3 250 grams, which is 3 kilograms 250 grams. And watch the zeros: 2 kilograms 30 grams is 2 030 grams, not 2 300. A thousand grams in a kilogram, every time.
visual_style: Whiteboard biscuit packets stacking onto a scale in quarter-kilogram steps; potato and onion bags adding in grams; a zero being placed carefully.
pacing: The biscuit puzzle, the quarter-kilogram reveal, a fast addition, then the zero trap.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and check the masses printed on five packets in your kitchen.
